subject: Proposal- Javascript client for R using nixysa framework

messages.author: 2e8e33d9d4028148
messages.subject: Proposal- Javascript client for R using nixysa framework
parts:
Hello everyone,

The web is becoming more and more dominant platform. That's why I
want to expose the idea of the cross-browser client for R using nixysa
project.

Nixysa is a framework that lets you write code in c++, then
generates NPAPI(Netscape Plug-in Application Programming Interface)
compatible code and, using scons, builds a plug-in on any platform, so
that you can use its functionality from JavaScript. Nixysa works with
most of the platforms and browsers.

The project idea is to create:
- custom R graphics driver targetting the HTML5 canvas tag,
forwarding low level drawing instructions to the dynamic page in real
time, so that we can use R graphics in the browser.
- static plug-in(R embedded into the plug-in) that takes R
instructions from JavaScript code and, using nixysa, returns the
result/code directly into the html/js document.(Rcpp and Rinside
frameworks)
- client for R running remotely.(using Rserve)

Advantages:
- full interactivity with R
- cross-platform and cross-browser support
- native HTML/JavaScript code (there is no need to install any other
plug-in)

Disadvantages:
- security

If you have any questions please don't hesitate to ask me.

Konstantin Gorodinskiy

As I've mentioned on the threads for all of the similar ideas where
you've posted a link to this, you need to:

* motivate the problem you are trying to solve
* describe what other existing efforts do and why they're not good
enough, or why you're not contributing to them
* give a firm roadmap that makes us confident you'll get the work
achieved in three months

Hadley

messages.author: 2e8e33d9d4028148
messages.subject: Re: Proposal- Javascript client for R using nixysa framework
parts:
- The goal of my project is to create an easy way to access R
functionality from web browser.

I want user to be able to write instructions like:
R rObj;//initialize the R-plugin in .js or .html file
rObj.eval(“x <- seq(0, 7, length=100)”);
rObj.eval(“y <- dlnorm(x)”);
rObj.eval(“plot(x,y,xlab="x",ylab="DLog(x)")”);

in js or html document, and to be able to get the plot within browser
with native HTML5/js code, without having to install any other plug-
ins or using applets.

- There is SNetscape package(http://www.omegahat.org/SNetscape/)
The problem there is that it uses Java applets to draw graphics. Today
with help of new HTML5 features such as canvas we can do complex
things in the browser without having to install additional packages.

Here is the example of drawing plot (sinus function) I wrote. It's
using HTML5 canvas tag:
http://gorodinskiy.org/plotExample/

- Suggested timeline is:
1. Implementing plug-in architecture that will accept R
instructions(in R syntax) and give
back result/code (1 week)
2. Wrapping R functionality into the plug-in (2-3 weeks)
3. Writing js layer to draw different graphics information and testing
them across all
browsers that support HTML 5 (1-2 week).
4. Modifying plug-in so to give back code to draw graphics to js/html
document(3 days)
5. Testing using different R instructions(2 weeks minimum)

Konstantin Gorodinskiy
